headline: Learning summary for 2026-09-08: moneyline record 1-1 (50.0%).

gates.note: Official picks require high model probability and strong setup quality. A high Lab Rating alone is not enough. (Market edge is no longer a gate -- a picked side with a lower market-implied probability than the model's read can still qualify, as long as market data exists for the game at all.)

findings.title: Official-pick discipline
findings.read: 2 moneyline picks were graded today. Record: 1-1 (50.0%).

findings.title: Probability gate
findings.read: No high-Lab, low-probability moneyline setups appeared in the graded official set.

findings.title: What's working: Lab Rating components
findings.read: Over 364 graded picks with a reconciling breakdown, pitching plan is the strongest working piece of Lab Rating right now -- picks scoring above its median win 65.7% of the time vs. 54.9% below (lift +10.8%, correlation to winning +0.111).

findings.title: What's not working: Lab Rating components
findings.read: bullpen -- correlation to winning -0.087, lift -4.6% over 364 picks. Currently not earning its points -- moves the score without moving the record. Bullpen no longer scores Lab Rating (removed 2026-08-30, folded into pitching plan) -- this is its pre-change record, not a live component.

findings.title: Bullpen learning
findings.read: Across all reviewed days, 16 graded moneyline picks carried a meaningful bullpen caution. Bullpen was removed from Lab Rating's own scoring on 2026-08-30 (folded into pitching plan) -- this caution count is a separate, still-live read from the bullpen-fatigue system, unaffected by that change. For reference, its PRE-CHANGE scoring history correlated -0.087 with winning over 364 picks (lift -4.6%). Currently not earning its points -- moves the score without moving the record.

findings.title: Pitcher learning
findings.read: No major starting-pitcher conflicts showed up in the graded moneyline set. Statistically, the pitching-plan component correlates +0.111 with winning over 364 picks (lift +10.8%).

findings.title: Rating calibration
findings.read: Actual win rate by Lab Rating band: 0-49 → 56.2% (n=137), 50-64 → 61.3% (n=119), 65-74 → 63.3% (n=60), 75-84 → 65.0% (n=40), 85-100 → 50.0% (n=8). Widest predicted-vs-actual gap is the 85-100 band (-22.1%). The top band has only 8 graded picks so far -- too few to trust its win rate yet, watch as the sample grows.

shadow_model.note: Only rows from the latest matching official/shadow model-version pair are compared. Promote nothing from a mixed-version sample.

attribution.note: Win rate by input tertile, pick-side relative. |spread| = high-band win rate minus low-band — bigger magnitude = the metric separates winners from losers harder, and deserves weight. Read direction too: a NEGATIVE spread on a should-be-positive factor is a red flag.

kprops.note: Bias = actual minus projection (positive means we under-project). Leans only counted at 0.7+ strikeout edges. Small samples early — a lean record means little before ~100 graded pitchers.

calibration.note: Shadow ledger for learning only — never part of the public record. Official picks stay the only published record.

Lab Rating's bullpen component score (retired 2026-08-30 -- pre-change history only): r=-0.070 (n=509) -- little to no relationship. Bottom quarter (0.00 to 4.26): 84-43 (66.1%). Top quarter (11.33 to 20.00): 70-58 (54.7%).

Lab Rating's pitching-plan component score: r=0.054 (n=509) -- little to no relationship. Bottom quarter (0.00 to 6.00): 75-52 (59.1%). Top quarter (20.00 to 40.00): 85-43 (66.4%).
Probability points bullpen risk moved this pick's number: r=-0.048 (n=509) -- little to no relationship. Bottom quarter (-0.14 to -0.03): 82-45 (64.6%). Top quarter (0.05 to 0.17): 72-56 (56.3%).
Pick tier (official / value watch / watchlist / pass): official_pick 31-17 (64.6%, n=48) vs. watchlist 47-30 (61.0%, n=77) vs. pass 221-154 (58.9%, n=375) vs. value_watch 4-5 (44.4%, n=9).

These are correlations across LyDia's own analyzed history, not causal proof and not a signal to change any model weight or gate on their own -- human review still required for any actual change.
